entries.title: Team Sports
entries.summary: Team sports need everyone to work together.
entries.body: In football, basketball or netball, everybody has a job. Passing the ball and moving your teammates into space is more useful than keeping the ball yourself. A good team listens to each other.
facts: Every player has a role in a team.
Listening to your teammates makes you stronger.

entries.title: Fair Play
entries.summary: Playing fair means following the rules.
entries.body: Good players tell the referee when they do something wrong. They wait for their turn, they do not cheat to win, and they say sorry when they make a mistake. Winning fairly feels better later.
facts: Telling the truth about a mistake is the honest thing to do.
A fair win feels better than a cheat.

entries.title: Swimming
entries.summary: Swimming is a skill everybody can learn.
entries.body: People float because the water pushes them up. Swimming needs confidence, practice and breathing control. Learning in shallow water with an adult nearby is the safest way to start.
facts: Your body floats because of buoyancy.
Practice and lessons help a lot.
Children should learn to swim with an adult nearby.

entries.title: Cycling
entries.summary: Cycling is fun exercise and a great way to travel.
entries.body: A bike needs three things to be safe: a helmet that fits, a check that the brakes and tyres work, and lights for evenings. Learning to ride takes practice, but most children learn in a day or two.
facts: A helmet must fit properly to protect you.
Check the brakes and tyres before you ride.
You need lights when riding in the dark.

entries.title: Board Games
entries.summary: Board games teach planning and patience.
entries.body: In a board game you follow rules, you take turns and you have to plan ahead. Games like chess teach you to think a few moves ahead, and games like Snakes and Ladders teach patience with good and bad luck.
facts: Board games teach planning and taking turns.
Chess teaches you to think ahead.
Even games with luck teach patience.

entries.title: Winning and Losing
entries.summary: How you win matters as much as winning.
entries.body: Everybody loses sometimes. What matters is how you handle it: try again, learn from what went wrong and cheer for your friends. A good sportsperson is happy for the team, not only for themselves.
facts: Losing happens to everybody, even champions.
Learning from a loss makes you better.
Cheering for friends is part of being a good sportsperson.

questions.prompt: Why is passing the ball useful?
questions.explanation: Passing moves your teammates and gives everyone a chance.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you make a mistake in a game?
questions.explanation: Telling the truth is what fair play means.

questions.prompt: Why do we float in water?
questions.explanation: Buoyancy pushes up on our bodies from below.

questions.prompt: What is the most important piece of safety gear when cycling?
questions.explanation: A properly fitting helmet protects your head.

questions.prompt: Which game teaches you to think a few moves ahead?
Even the best players lose sometimes.
questions.explanation: Losing is part of sport, and how you handle it matters.

options: Following the rules and being kind
questions.explanation: Good sportsmanship means playing by the rules and treating others well.

questions.prompt: What do we call a game played on a board with pieces?
questions.explanation: It is called a board game.

questions.prompt: What should you check before a bike ride?
questions.explanation: Checking the brakes and tyres keeps you safe.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you lose?
questions.explanation: Learning from a loss makes you better next time.
